# Acknowledged unreleased changes: changes to a package's shipped files since its release that ship nothing a consumer
# sees, such as comments only, or build settings that produce the same result. A release may leave such a package at its
# released version.
#
# C-Prepare-Release, C-SimulateRelease and the Create Releases workflow refuse while a package that the release doesn't
# release has shipped files that changed since its release tag, unless the changes are acknowledged here. For a package
# named here, they look only at the changes after the later of its release tag and the commit named here.
#
# One line per package: <PackageId> <full commit id> <reason>, the commit being the one up to which the package's
# changes are acknowledged. C-Prepare-Release or C-SimulateRelease -Acknowledge <PackageId> -Reason '<why>' writes the
# line for HEAD, and C-Prepare-Release removes it when it prepares the package's release. Comments go here, above the
# lines. .github/scripts/lib/UnreleasedChanges.ps1 reads the file.
